adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 4 svarita = 10, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 10 marks (verified programmatically). All three also independently found the same hard case: the sixth anudatta bar is set ~14-16 px BELOW the other five (y2076-2086 vs y2059-2073) because the printer had to clear the vocalic-R hook of the N+NR conjunct. S1 corroborated the habit on line 3 of the same leaf, where bars under TR and VR are dropped the same way. Two aksara identities were disputed, both ADJUDICATED FROM THE SCAN by side-by-side composite against controls taken from the same printed line: (1) word 4: AYAM (S1) vs AGRAM (S2, S3). Adopted AGRAM. The disputed glyph was composited against the certain YA of word 3 on the same line: the certain YA is a compact left bowl with a thin crescent counter joining the stem horizontally at the foot, whereas the disputed glyph has an open upper-left hook plus a prominent bold diagonal descending below the body line - a subscript RA. Majority and image agree. (2) word 3: ANAYADVACO (S1, S2) vs ANAYANVACO (S3). Adopted ANAYANVACO, OVERRIDING the 2-1 majority. The conjunct at x966-1070 was composited against plain NA (x1550-1628), plain DA (x2195-2262) and plain VA (x2128-2196) from the same line. The conjunct's upper member is a left blob with a horizontal bar running right and white above it - identical to plain NA - while plain DA on this line is a hook curving down-left with a rounded terminal and NO rightward bar. The lower member matches plain VA. S1 had justified DVA by claiming the upper member repeats the left wedge plus rightward bar of the plain DA, but the DA on this line has no rightward bar at all; that feature is diagnostic of NA. Both S1 and S2 had already flagged this conjunct as their least certain glyph. Neither disputed locus affects any mark tuple.
boundary_interpretation: The sirorekha never fully breaks inside a printed word on this line: projecting rows 1951-1968 column-wise, the within-word minimum is 10-16 inked rows out of 18 and never 0, so headline breaks could not be used to cut words. I therefore cut on white gaps in the below-headline body: inter-word gaps measure 39-46 px (409|449, 566|607, 678|720, 1210|1249, 1431|1470, 1744|1784, 1903|1942, 2015|2061, 2563|2606) while every gap inside a word is <=22 px. Word list (0-based): 0 dhiitii x187-409, 1 vaa x449-566, 2 ye x607-678, 3 anayanvaaco x720-1210, 4 agram x1249-1431, 5 manasaa x1470-1744, 6 vaa x1784-1903, 7 ye x1942-2015, 8 avagraha+vadannrtaani x2061-2563, 9 danda x2606-2622, 10 double danda x2875-2912, 11 numeral x2961-3009, 12 double danda x3059-3095. The gap between the avagraha (x2061-2110) and va (x2122-) is only 12 px, i.e. intra-word by the same criterion, so I read avagraha+vadannrtaani as ONE printed word (index 8); the avagraha is not an aksara, so va is aksara_index 0 in that word. Boundary calls, mark by mark: (a) x226 anudatta - dhiitii splits into dhii x187-288 (dha body 187-269 plus the ii-vertical 272-285) and tii x305-396; the bar spans 208-244, wholly inside dhii and 60 px left of the divide -> dhii. (b) x872 svarita - na occupies x825-901 with its stem at 873-885 and ya begins at 902; the stroke (867-876) stands on na's stem, not over ya -> na, index 1. (c) x1014 anudatta - ya ends 965, the nvaa cluster runs 966-1091 (half-na 966-990, va 990-1035, aa-stroke 1042-1069), co begins 1092; the bar 995-1033 sits under va inside nvaa -> nvaa, index 3, not ya and not co. (d) x1400 anudatta - a occupies 1249-1353 (stem 1327-1340), gram occupies 1354-1431 (stem 1407-1421); the bar 1381-1419 lies entirely right of the divide -> gram, index 1; the anusvara dot 1399-1420 sits over the same aksara and is not an accent. (e) x1607 svarita - ma 1470-1546, na 1557-1619 (stem 1606-1619), saa 1627-1744; the stroke 1602-1612 stands on na's stem -> na, index 1. (f) x2177 svarita - the avagraha ends 2110, va runs 2133-2187 (stem 2174-2187), da begins 2202; the stroke 2172-2182 is on va's stem -> va, index 0. (g) x2311 anudatta - da ends ~2270, the nnr conjunct runs ~2258-2344 (stem 2315-2331, r-hook 2300-2344), taa begins 2346; the bar 2293-2329 is directly under the conjunct -> nnr, index 2. (h) x2543 svarita - the final ni cluster is 2460-2557: the i-matra's vertical is on the LEFT at 2464-2477 and its arc ends at 2522, while na's stem is 2540-2554; the stroke 2538-2547 stands 16 px right of the arc's end and directly on na's stem, so it is an accent and not part of the matra -> ni, index 4.
notes: MAGNIFICATION: read the two supplied ~1:1 segment crops first, then measured the source raster directly with PIL (row and column ink profiles at grey threshold 128, plus 8-connected component extents), then re-rendered my own crops of the same line from the same leaf at 2.8x to 12x for visual confirmation of every mark and carrier. Component geometry was re-run at thresholds 150 and 170 in case a faintly inked mark was being lost; nothing new of accent shape appeared. MARK MORPHOLOGY: the six anudattas are 36-39 px wide and 9-11 px tall, fill 0.76-0.92 - dense flat dashes, distinctly wider than tall. The four svaritas are 9-12 px wide and 30-36 px tall, fill 0.85-0.96 - narrow uprights, each standing on the right-hand stem of its consonant. A column-by-column pixel map confirms all four svaritas are the same object; two of them (x2172-2182 and x2538-2547) merge with their word component only because the sirorekha itself drifts about 5 px lower toward the right end of the line, not because they are letter parts. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES, by shape: (1) the anusvara over gram at x1399-1420, 22x24 px, h/w 1.09, a filled lozenge - a dot about as wide as it is tall, not an upright stroke. (2) Six above-headline vowel signs, all wide and curved, 54-69 px across, h/w about 0.5: ii over dhii x229-283, ii over tii x338-391, e over ye x609-667, o over co x1122-1190, e over the second ye x1944-2001, i over the final ni x2463-2522. (3) The da tail in vadan, x2239-2265, 27x20, fill 0.38, curved and continuous with the body. (4) The r-vocalic descender under the nnr conjunct, x2300-2344, 45x39, fill 0.60, a curved hook continuous with the body - not a straight dash. (5) Sub-10 px specks: x2432-2437 at the foot of the aa-stroke in taa, and several 2-8 px fragments at y>=2091 which are the truncated tops of the NEXT line's glyphs. (6) The faint grey shapes between the danda (x2622) and the double danda (x2875) are verso show-through: no pixel there falls below grey 170. LINE ATTRIBUTION: the central trap does not bite on this line, and I verified that rather than assuming it - rows 1859-1915 are line-wide zero ink, so there is no line-above bar band in my gutter at all. Everything I counted below the body sits 25-52 px under my own baseline and 42-95 px above the next line's first ink. THE ONE HARD CALL: the anudatta at x2293-2329 sits at y2077-2086, about 16 px lower than the other five bars (y2059-2072). I accepted it because (i) its shape is an exact twin of the other five (37x10 px, fill 0.92), (ii) it is bounded by line-wide zero-ink rows 2075-2076 above and 2087-2090 below, so it is a free-standing mark and not the tail of the r-hook that ends at y2074, and (iii) it cannot belong to the next line, whose first ink is at y2091 and whose own bar band would lie near y2240. The obvious explanation for the drop is that the printer had to set it clear of the r-vocalic hook immediately above it. READING NOTES: the standalone a is read per the fount note - it looks like shra or vocalic r in this 1856 type - and it occurs twice, at x720-824 and x1249-1353. Short i versus long ii was decided by which side the matra's vertical sits on: right for ii (dhii: arc 229-283 with its vertical at 272-285), left for i (ni: arc 2463-2522 with its vertical at 2464-2477); that distinction is what makes the upright at x2538-2547 an accent rather than an ii-stem. The least certain glyph on the line is the stacked conjunct at about x2258-2344, which I read as half-na over na with the r-vocalic sign below (nnr); at 12x it shows two stacked na-like elements, a stem, and the hook. I did not reconstruct the line from memory; where the ink and expectation could have diverged (the mark over gram, which at low magnification looks like an accent) I followed the ink and recorded it as anusvara. The terminal numeral is a closed bowl with a straight stem descending on the right, i.e. 1, not 9. As printed there is a wide blank of about 250 px (x2622-2875) between the single danda and the double danda; I have written it as a single space.
